chunks: And from him (Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id) from Muhammad ibn Fudayl who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the limit/time by which if a man reaches it, he has attained the Hajj. He said: 'If he arrives at Jam' while the people are at al-Mash'ar before the sunrise, he has attained the Hajj and his Umrah is not separate. But if he does not arrive at Jam' until the sun has risen, then it is a separate Umrah and he has no Hajj. If he wishes, he may stay, and if he wishes, he may return, and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year.'

key_terms.الْمَشْعَر: Al-Mash'ar, referring to al-Mash'ar al-Haram (the Sacred Monument/Mount Arafat area) where pilgrims stand in prayer.
key_terms.جَمْع: Jam', the valley between Mina and al-Mash'ar where pilgrims stay before proceeding to Mecca.
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْس: Sunrise, the specific temporal marker for the validity of the stay at Jam'.
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَة: A separate Umrah, indicating that the Hajr ritual was performed outside its valid time window.
key_terms.قَابِل: Next year, referring to the obligation to repeat the Hajj if the condition is not met.

ai.seo_question: What is the time limit for staying at Jam' to validly complete the Hajj ritual?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the critical temporal boundary for the stay at Jam' (Muzdalifah), distinguishing between a complete Hajj and a standalone Umrah based on arrival before or after sunrise. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the precise timing of rituals, noting that missing this window invalidates the Hajj obligation for the current year, requiring the pilgrim to either stay and perform Umrah or depart and return the following year. This ruling underscores the importance of synchronizing human action with the natural signs of God in maintaining the validity of the pilgrimage.
